$comment: The canonical SDK surface: what an implementation must expose to call itself an IAES SDK. SDK_SURFACE.md is the reasoning. tests/test_surface.py reads this file and fails when a declaration stops matching the code, so a gap cannot be closed or opened without the declaration moving with it.

status.notice: Changing this file does not change what an IAES event is. It changes what an implementation must offer to call itself an IAES SDK.

naming.rule: The same word, in each language's convention. Never a different verb.

conventions.cpp: camelCase methods on a class named for the capability group
conventions.node_red: one node per capability, named iaes-<capability>

incorrect: from_dict vs fromJSON -- different verbs, not different casing
Client vs IaesClient -- the type is named differently, not spelled differently

input.field_names: exactly the schema's, in every language
input.container: idiomatic per language -- dataclass, object literal, struct, form fields
input.two_doors: a typed constructor, and construction from a plain object
input.extra_fields: carried through; never stripped, never rejected
input.optional_fields: omitting and passing null behave identically
input.lists: a list is of EVENTS, never of fields. publish([a,b,c]) yes; Measurement([...]) no.

errors.requirement: Failure must look the same across implementations.
validation_failure_reports: the path of the offending field
errors.note: Python raises ValidationError and TypeScript has IaesClientError, and they do not do the same thing. This is the least-examined part of the surface and the most consequential for someone moving between languages.

build.what: construct an event of a published type

from_object.what: construct an event from a plain object
from_object.note: Two verbs today. The canonical name is from_object; both existing names become deprecated aliases rather than disappearing.

validate.what: check an event against its published schema, reporting the failing field path
validate.note: Measured 2026-09-06: three of five have it, and the one that does not is the TypeScript SDK -- which is the one the two flow runtimes depend on.

compute_content_hash.what: the digest the specification defines: SHA-256 over canonical JSON with sorted keys, first 16 hex characters
compute_content_hash.note: Must agree across languages. The C++ implementation shipped FNV-1a over insertion order until 2026-09-06, so the same reading hashed differently depending on which SDK produced it. Its conformance is now checked against digests produced by the Python SDK.

schema_uri_for.what: derive the schema URI from an event type
schema_uri_for.note: This is what dataschema carries. Neither flow runtime emits dataschema today, though both depend on a TypeScript SDK that can derive it.

route.what: separate events by type using only the published vocabulary
route.note: Required where the platform's shape makes it meaningful -- a flow runtime. A library caller does this with a switch, which is why its absence in Python and TypeScript is not a gap.

vocabulary.note: All of them. The flow runtimes take theirs from @iaes/sdk rather than exposing a node, which is the platform's idiom and counts as present.

not_capabilities.publish: Sending an event somewhere is not part of this standard: IAES defines no transport, no endpoint contract and no delivery negotiation, so there is nothing for a second implementation to conform to. A function that sends is a client for a particular server and belongs to that server's package. It becomes a capability the day a transport binding exists.
not_capabilities.detect: Deadbands, thresholds and assigning a severity when one is crossed put a value on a field and interpret a number. That is an implementation's judgment.
not_capabilities.device_profiles: An equipment catalog. GOVERNANCE.md section 1.2 excludes these by name, thresholds included.
not_capabilities.transport_clients: A Modbus or MQTT client is neither standard nor product -- it is generic plumbing, like an HTTP library, and claims neither side.
not_capabilities.protocol_bindings: node-red-contrib-iaes ships an iaes-sparkplug node. A binding maps IAES onto one wire protocol; it is useful and it is not part of the surface every implementation must offer.

implementations.$comment: Declared gaps, not silent ones. An absent capability that nobody declared is indistinguishable from one nobody thought of, and that is how five platforms arrived at five different surfaces. Checked by tests/test_surface.py.

python.note: route is not a gap: a library caller uses a switch.

typescript.note: The only SDK that cannot check an event against its schema, and the one both flow runtimes depend on.

gaps: build: work_order_intent, completion, spare_part_usage, sensor_registration, hierarchy
cpp.note: A microcontroller runtime, deliberately narrow. Its conformance is checked in its own repository's CI, not here, so tests/test_surface.py does not verify this row -- which is itself a gap, and stated rather than left implied.
